parole.testo: From Ottoman Turkish فیلو (filo, “line of battle”), from Venetan filo (“line”), from Latin filum.

From Ottoman Turkish فورطنه (furtuna, fırtuna, fırtına), from Venetan fortuna, from Latin fortūna. The Latin word meant any sort of luck, good or bad, but among sailors the word became specialized to mean a particular kind of bad luck, a storm. parole.significato: brine, pickle, water saturated or strongly impregnated with salt, generally used for pickling
parole.testo: Inherited from Ottoman Turkish سالاموره (salamura, “brine”), from Venetan salamora (“brine”), ultimately from Latin salimuria (“brine, pickle”).
